value.body: A three-year postgraduate dental degree after BDS. Students specialise in one of the recognised dental specialities and complete clinical training and a dissertation. It is regulated by the Dental Council of India (DCI).

items.label: Specialities
items.note: E.g. Orthodontics, Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery, Endodontics, Prosthodontics, Periodontology, Paediatric Dentistry

value.title: How you get in
value.body: BDS from a DCI-recognised college, with internship completed and registration with a State Dental Council. Admission is through NEET-MDS (conducted by NBEMS), followed by MCC counselling for the all-India quota and state counselling for the rest.

value.title: At a glance
items: Most MDS seats are in private colleges, where fees can be high; government seats are far fewer.
An MDS is generally needed for teaching posts in dental colleges.
Speciality choice depends on rank — clinical branches fill first.
Many MDS graduates go into private practice, alone or in group clinics.
